cuestionario.title: Cuestionario Consolidado — Evidence 6
cuestionario.instructions: Answer all 25 questions. Choose the correct option (a, b, or c) unless the question says True or False. You have 90 minutes. No materials, no Word Wall, no Communication Card.

sections.source_text: Tools Every Diesel Technician Needs (adapted from Popular Mechanics, A1.1)

items.q: What is the main topic of the article?
items.answer_explanation: The article title and content focus on the essential tools every diesel technician needs in the workshop.

items.q: A torque wrench is used to ___.

options.b: apply the correct force to a bolt

items.answer_explanation: The article explains that the torque wrench applies a specific, measured force (torque) to bolts and fasteners.

items.q: True or False: The ratchet works well in large spaces.
items.answer_explanation: FALSE. The text states the ratchet is fast in tight spaces — it is designed for confined areas where a full wrench swing is not possible.

items.q: Where does a technician keep tools organized?
items.answer_explanation: The article identifies the toolbox as the primary place where a technician keeps tools organized and accessible.

items.q: What does 'calibration' mean in the article?

options.b: Checking that the tool is accurate

items.answer_explanation: In the article context, calibration refers to the process of verifying and adjusting a tool so that its measurements are accurate.

items.q: What is a 'workbench'?

options.b: A flat surface to work on

items.answer_explanation: A workbench is a sturdy, flat surface where technicians place parts, tools, and equipment while performing repairs.

items.q: 'Hazard' means ___.
items.answer_explanation: A hazard is anything that poses a risk of injury, damage, or danger in the workshop environment.

items.q: Which of these is PPE?
items.answer_explanation: PPE stands for Personal Protective Equipment. Safety goggles protect the eyes and are worn on the body — unlike tools (torque wrench) or equipment (floor jack).

items.q: A 'work order' is ___.

options.a: an instruction to lift a vehicle
options.b: a document describing a repair task

items.answer_explanation: A work order is a formal document that describes the repair or maintenance task to be completed, including details about the vehicle and the work required.

items.q: 'Preventive maintenance' means ___.
items.answer_explanation: Preventive maintenance is the practice of regularly servicing equipment on a schedule to prevent unexpected breakdowns — as opposed to corrective maintenance, which fixes things after they break.

sections.source: Imperatives, There is/are, Prepositions of place (S3)

items.q: Which sentence is an imperative?
items.answer_explanation: An imperative gives a direct command or instruction. 'Check the floor jack.' begins with the base verb and has no subject — the hallmark of an imperative sentence. Option (a) is a simple present statement; option (c) is passive voice.

items.q: Complete: '___ a spill near the bay door.'
items.answer_explanation: 'A spill' is singular, so we use 'There is.' 'There are' requires a plural noun. 'Is there' would form a question, but this sentence is a statement (no question mark).

items.q: Complete: 'The tools ___ in the toolbox.'
items.answer_explanation: 'Tools' is plural, so the correct verb is 'are.' We use 'is' with singular nouns and 'has' is not used for location.

items.q: Complete: 'The fire extinguisher is ___ the bay door.'
items.answer_explanation: From the Bay 2 Safety Briefing: Carlos says 'The fire extinguisher is always next to the bay door.' The preposition 'next to' indicates proximity/beside — the extinguisher is mounted on the wall beside the door for quick access.

items.q: Which sentence has a correct preposition of place?

options.a: The wrench is near of the workbench.
options.b: The wrench is on the workbench.
options.c: The wrench is in front the workbench.

items.answer_explanation: Option (b) is correct: 'on' is a standard preposition of place meaning 'resting on the surface of.' Option (a) is wrong because 'near' does not take 'of.' Option (c) is wrong because the correct form is 'in front of' (missing 'of').

sections.source: Bay 2 Safety Briefing dialogue (Carlos Mendoza / Valentina Cruz, 18 turns)

items.q: In the dialogue, who is the supervisor?
items.answer_explanation: Carlos Mendoza is the Lead Technician/Supervisor. He gives instructions and conducts the safety briefing. Valentina is the apprentice receiving instructions.

items.q: What PPE does Carlos ask Valentina to wear?
items.answer_explanation: Carlos says: 'First, put on your PPE. Gloves and goggles.' He specifies both items — not just one.

items.q: Where is the oil spill in the dialogue?
items.answer_explanation: Carlos says: 'There is an oil spill near the bay door.' The preposition 'near' + location 'bay door' are both stated explicitly.

items.q: Carlos says the fire extinguisher is always ___.
items.answer_explanation: Carlos states: 'The fire extinguisher is always next to the bay door.' The word 'always' emphasizes this is a fixed, known location for safety equipment.

items.q: What does Valentina say at the end of the dialogue?
items.answer_explanation: Valentina closes the dialogue with: 'Checklist complete. Bay 2 is ready.' This confirms she has completed all safety checks and the bay is cleared for work.

items.q: Carlos says: 'Check the torque wrench.' What communication function is this?
items.answer_explanation: F1 — Dar instrucciones. The imperative form ('Check...') is the grammatical marker for giving instructions. Carlos, as supervisor, directs Valentina to perform a specific action.

items.q: Valentina says: 'Can I have the socket set?' What function?
items.answer_explanation: F2 — Solicitar herramientas. 'Can I have...?' is a polite request structure. Additional examples: 'I need the ratchet,' 'Could you pass me the wrench?'

items.q: 'There is a spill near Bay 2.' What function?
items.answer_explanation: F3 — Describir condiciones. The structure 'There is + noun + preposition of place' is used to describe the current state or conditions of the workspace. It tells what exists and where.

items.q: Santiago says: 'Bay 3 is ready, Carlos.' What function?
items.answer_explanation: F4 — Reportar al supervisor. Santiago addresses Carlos by name and uses Present Simple to communicate the status of his assigned bay. This is a classic upward report: technician informs supervisor that a task is complete.

items.q: Valentina says: 'Got it. I'll do it now.' What function?
items.answer_explanation: F5 — Confirmar comprension. 'Got it' signals that the listener has understood. 'I'll do it now' adds commitment to action. Other markers: 'Understood,' 'Copy that,' 'Will do.'

teacher_talk.opening: Good morning, everyone. Welcome to Session 6 — 'Prove What You Know.' Today is special. This is your chance to show everything you have learned across all five sessions. I am proud of how far you have come, and I know you are ready for this.
teacher_talk.instruction: Before we begin, I have your Evidence 5 results from last session. I will hand them back now with individual comments. Please read my notes — they are personal and meant to help you. Take two minutes to look at your feedback, then put the sheet away. We will need clear desks for what comes next.
teacher_talk.transition: Now. The Cuestionario Consolidado. Here is what you need to know: 25 questions. Five sections — Reading, Vocabulary, Grammar, Listening, and Language Functions. You have 90 minutes. This is a closed-materials assessment. That means no Communication Card, no Word Wall, no notes. Just you and what you know. I am going to distribute the forms face down. Do not turn them over until I say 'Begin.'
teacher_talk.icq: Quick check before we start. Can you use your Communication Card during the quiz? ... No. Can you use the Word Wall? ... No. How many questions are there? ... 25. How much time do you have? ... 90 minutes. Perfect. You are ready.

activities.activity: Return Evidence 5 (Escala de estimacion No 5) with individual written comments. Students read feedback silently.
activities.facilitation_note: Have the Escala sheets pre-sorted alphabetically so distribution is fast. Write at least one specific positive comment and one growth point per student before the session.

activities.activity: Cuestionario format overview: 25 items, 5 sections, 90 minutes, closed materials. Cover or turn the Word Wall to face the wall. Collect Communication Cards from desks.
activities.facilitation_note: Covering the Word Wall is a visible signal that this is a formal assessment. Students take it more seriously when the environment changes. If the Word Wall cannot be covered, place blank chart paper over it.

activities.activity: Distribute Cuestionario forms face down. Students write name and date on the front page (visible without flipping). Confirm everyone has a pen/pencil.
activities.facilitation_note: Walk the room to verify all students have writing materials. Have 3-4 spare pencils ready. A small thing, but a student without a pencil loses confidence before they even start.

activities.activity: ICQ sequence. Confirm conditions. Answer any procedural questions (not content questions). Countdown: 'Flip your papers. Begin.'
activities.facilitation_note: Keep your voice calm and confident during the ICQ. Your tone sets the emotional temperature of the room. If you sound stressed, they will be stressed.

plan_b.risk: Evidence 5 feedback triggers emotional reactions or long questions that delay the Cuestionario start
plan_b.mitigation: Set a timer for 8 minutes. At 07:08, say: 'I see you have questions about your feedback — and those are important. Let us talk about them after the Cuestionario, during the review. Right now, let us focus forward.' This validates the emotion while protecting the timeline.

teacher_talk.instruction: You may now begin. Work quietly and individually. Read each question carefully. If you are unsure about an answer, mark your best choice and move on — you can come back to it if you have time. I will give you a 15-minute warning and a 5-minute warning before time is up.

activities.activity: Final instructions + name/date verification. Students begin reading the Cuestionario. Instructor circulates to confirm everyone has started.
activities.facilitation_note: Some students will freeze when they see 25 questions. Walk by them calmly, point to Question 1, and whisper: 'Start here. One question at a time.' That small gesture can unlock a paralyzed student.

activities.activity: Silent individual work — Cuestionario Consolidado. NO materials open. Instructor monitors silently (no hovering).
activities.facilitation_note: Position yourself where you can see all students but are not looming over anyone. A seat at the front corner works well. Avoid reading over shoulders — it creates anxiety. Your job during the 90 minutes is to be a calm, steady presence.

activities.activity: 15-minute warning: 'You have fifteen minutes remaining. If you have not answered every question, go back and make your best choice for each one. No blank answers.'
activities.facilitation_note: Say this once, clearly, then return to your seat. Do not repeat it or add pressure.

activities.activity: 5-minute warning: 'Five minutes. Finish the question you are on and review any you skipped.'
activities.facilitation_note: Watch for students who are still writing frantically. If someone is clearly distressed, make a note to check in during the break — but do not intervene now.

activities.activity: Time called. 'Pens down, please. Turn your Cuestionario face down on your desk.' Collect ALL forms immediately — walk row by row.
activities.facilitation_note: CRITICAL: Collect every single form before any discussion happens. If a student says 'Wait, one more second' — be firm but kind: 'I know, but time is time. You did great.' Do not allow corrections after the call.

activities.activity: Cognitive break + decompression. Students stand up, stretch. Brief pair share (30 seconds each): 'How did you feel about the Reading section? Thumbs up, sideways, or down.' No answers discussed — feelings only.
activities.facilitation_note: This pair share is deliberately emotional, not academic. It lets students release tension without spoiling the answer review. Thumbs up/sideways/down gives you a quick read of the room's confidence level per section.

formative_checkpoint.method: Thumbs up/sideways/down per section — instructor scans and mentally notes which sections caused the most 'sideways' or 'down' signals to adjust pacing in WHILE-B

differentiation.fast_finishers: Students who finish early: sit quietly, review their answers, or read silently (a book from their bag — NOT course materials). They may NOT leave the room or use phones.
differentiation.more_support: If a student appears stuck from the very beginning (not writing after 10 minutes), approach quietly and whisper: 'Read question 1 out loud to yourself, very quietly. What do you think?' This activates a different processing channel without giving away answers.

plan_b.risk: Audio equipment fails for the Listening section (students need to recall from memory, but some may expect to hear the dialogue again)
plan_b.mitigation: The Cuestionario tests recall — students are NOT supposed to hear the dialogue again during the quiz. However, if students protest, clarify: 'These questions test what you remember from our sessions. You do not need to hear the dialogue again — trust your memory.' If the group is genuinely confused, you may read each Listening question stem aloud (question only, not dialogue) to provide auditory support.

teacher_talk.transition: Great work, everyone. Take 15 minutes — stretch, get water, use the restroom. When you come back, we will go through every single answer together. No quiz talk during the break, please.

break.instructor_task: Use the 15 minutes to do a quick visual scan of the collected Cuestionarios. Do NOT grade them — just flip through 5-6 forms to spot obvious patterns: Are students consistently missing a particular section? Did anyone leave large sections blank? This gives you a sense of where to spend more explanation time in WHILE-B.
break.facilitation_note: Resist the urge to start grading. You need to be fully present for the review. A quick scan for patterns is enough. Also: eat something and drink water yourself. You have been 'on' for two hours.

teacher_talk.instruction: Welcome back. Now comes my favorite part — we go through every question together. I will read the question, you call out what you chose, and then I reveal the correct answer with an explanation. This is not about right or wrong — it is about understanding. Your forms are already collected, so relax. This is pure learning.

activities.activity: Review Reading questions. Read each question aloud. Students call out their answers. Reveal correct answer. Explain why.

answer_review.explanation: The article is called 'Tools Every Diesel Technician Needs' — the title itself tells us the main topic is essential tools, not safety rules or cleaning.
The text says the torque wrench 'applies the correct force to a bolt.' 'Force' in technical English often means torque — the turning power applied to a fastener.
The text says: 'The ratchet is fast in tight spaces.' Tight, not large. The ratchet's short swing arc is what makes it useful in confined areas where a full wrench rotation is impossible.
The article mentions the toolbox as the place where a technician keeps tools organized. A workbench is for working on — the toolbox is for storing.
Calibration means checking that a tool is accurate — making sure a torque wrench reads 50 Nm when it is actually applying 50 Nm. It is about precision, not cleaning or replacing.

activities.facilitation_note: For R3 (True/False), pause after revealing FALSE. Ask: 'Who can tell me the exact word from the text?' When someone says 'tight,' celebrate it: 'Exactly. One word makes the difference between true and false. That is why reading carefully matters.'

activities.activity: Review Vocabulary questions. For each term, give a brief real-world diesel workshop example.

answer_review.explanation: A workbench is a flat surface. Think of it as your workspace — where you lay out parts, inspect components, write on your checklist. It is not a storage container (that is the toolbox) and not a type of wrench.
A hazard is something dangerous. In the workshop: an oil spill is a hazard because you can slip. A loose cable is a hazard because you can trip. Always: hazard = danger.
PPE is Personal Protective Equipment — things you WEAR on your body to stay safe. Safety goggles go on your face. A torque wrench is a tool, a floor jack is equipment — you do not wear them.
A work order is a document. Think of it as the 'recipe' for a repair job — it tells you what vehicle, what problem, what to do, and when. It lives on paper or a screen, not on a floor jack.

Preventive maintenance is regular care BEFORE something breaks. Think of changing oil every 10,000 km — the engine is fine, but you maintain it to keep it fine. Corrective maintenance is the opposite: fixing something that already broke.

activities.facilitation_note: When reviewing V5, draw a quick T-chart on the board: 'Preventive = BEFORE it breaks' vs. 'Corrective = AFTER it breaks.' This visual distinction is powerful and reinforces the Toolbelt 20.

activities.activity: Review Grammar questions. Reference the color-coded board from S3 (Imperatives=red, There is/are=blue, Prepositions=green).

answer_review.explanation: An imperative starts with the base verb and has no visible subject — the 'you' is implied. 'Check the floor jack.' = imperative (red). 'I check...' = statement. 'The floor jack is checked.' = passive voice.
'A spill' is one spill — singular. So: 'There IS a spill.' If it were 'spills' (plural), we would say 'There ARE spills.' Singular = is. Plural = are. Blue grammar.
'Tools' is plural — more than one tool. Plural nouns take 'are.' 'The tools ARE in the toolbox.' If it were one tool: 'The tool IS in the toolbox.' Blue grammar again.
This comes straight from the dialogue: 'The fire extinguisher is always NEXT TO the bay door.' Not on top of it, not under it — beside it. 'Next to' is green grammar — a preposition of place.

'On the workbench' is correct. 'Near OF' is wrong — 'near' never takes 'of.' 'In front THE workbench' is wrong — the correct form is 'in front OF the workbench.' Prepositions are precise — one missing word changes everything.

activities.facilitation_note: If the S3 color-coded board is still posted, uncover it now and point to each color as you review. If it was taken down, quickly sketch three columns: RED (imperatives), BLUE (there is/are), GREEN (prepositions). Visual anchors reactivate S3 memory.

activities.activity: Review Listening questions. Re-read the relevant dialogue line aloud for each question.

answer_review.explanation: Carlos Mendoza is the supervisor — he is the Lead Technician who gives instructions throughout the Bay 2 briefing. Valentina is the apprentice. Santiago is another technician mentioned elsewhere.
[Read aloud] Carlos says: 'First, put on your PPE. Gloves AND goggles.' Both. Not just gloves, not just goggles — both together. Listen for the word 'and' — it connects two items.
[Read aloud] 'There is an oil spill near the bay door.' Near the bay door — not under the workbench, not in the toolbox. The preposition 'near' tells us the location.
[Read aloud] 'The fire extinguisher is always next to the bay door.' The word 'always' is important — it means this is a fixed location, not temporary. Safety equipment has a permanent place.

[Read aloud] Valentina's final line: 'Checklist complete. Bay 2 is ready.' This is how the dialogue ends — with confirmation that all checks are done and the bay is safe for work. A professional closure.

activities.facilitation_note: Read each dialogue line aloud in character — use a slightly different tone for Carlos (firm, supervisory) vs. Valentina (responsive, confident). Students light up when they 'hear' the dialogue again. It validates their memory.

activities.activity: Review Language Functions questions. Name the function in both English and Spanish. Give one additional example per function.

answer_review.explanation: F1 — Giving instructions / Dar instrucciones. The imperative 'Check the torque wrench' is a direct command. Another example: 'Clean the workbench before you leave.' Imperative = instruction.

F2 — Requesting tools/help / Solicitar herramientas. 'Can I have the socket set?' is a polite request. Another example: 'I need the floor jack for Bay 3.' The key structures are 'Can I have...' and 'I need...'

F3 — Describing conditions / Describir condiciones. 'There is a spill near Bay 2' uses 'There is' + noun + preposition of place. It describes what exists in the workspace. Another example: 'There are tools on the workbench.'

F4 — Reporting to supervisor / Reportar al supervisor. Santiago says 'Bay 3 is ready, Carlos.' He addresses the supervisor by name and communicates a status update. Another example: 'Carlos, the inspection is complete.'

F5 — Confirming understanding / Confirmar comprension. 'Got it. I'll do it now.' shows Valentina understood the instruction and will act on it. Other markers: 'Understood,' 'Copy that,' 'Will do.' Confirmation closes the communication loop.

activities.facilitation_note: After LF5, pause and say: 'Five functions. Five ways to communicate in a real diesel workshop. You learned these in Session 5 — and today you proved you know them.' Let the moment land. This connects the quiz to real professional competence.

formative_checkpoint.method: Quick hand count: 'How many of you got 5 out of 5 on this section? 4 out of 5? 3?' — This gives the instructor a real-time sense of performance distribution and tells students where they stand without waiting for formal grades.

differentiation.fast_finishers: Students who clearly mastered a section: invite them to give the explanation for one question ('Who wants to explain why G4 is c?'). This builds leadership and deepens their understanding through teaching.
differentiation.more_support: For sections where many students struggled: slow down, re-read the source text or dialogue line twice, and use the board to write key words. If the Grammar section was weak, spend an extra 2 minutes on the color-coded chart.

plan_b.risk: Review runs long and exceeds 75 minutes
plan_b.mitigation: Monitor time per section: aim for 15 min each. If Reading takes 18 minutes, compress Vocabulary to 12 by giving shorter explanations for items most students got correct. The key is to spend more time on questions that caused confusion, less on ones everyone nailed. Have a visible timer or clock.

while_c.label: Gap Cards + Skills Reflection

teacher_talk.instruction: Now I want to take you back to the very first day. Session 1. Remember your Gap Cards? You wrote down things you did NOT know — things you could not do yet. I have them right here. Let us see how much has changed.

activities.activity: Gap Cards preview. Instructor brings out the plastified Gap Cards from S1. Reads 3 statements aloud (selected for maximum contrast — things students clearly could NOT do in S1 but CAN do now). After each statement: 'Could you answer this NOW?' Show of hands. Celebrate growth with genuine enthusiasm.
sample_statements: 'Name three types of PPE used in a diesel workshop.' — Could you answer this now?
'Use There is/There are to describe a workshop condition.' — Could you answer this now?
'Give an instruction using an imperative verb.' — Could you answer this now?
activities.facilitation_note: This is the most emotionally powerful moment in S6. Choose Gap Card statements that will produce a unanimous 'YES' from the class. When every hand goes up, let the silence hang for one second before you say anything. They need to feel their own growth. Then: 'Look at your hands. Every single one of you. That is six sessions of hard work, and it shows.' NOTE: Do NOT redistribute the Gap Cards — that happens in S8. Today is preview only.

activities.activity: Skills Reflection: 'Then vs. Now' chart. Students complete a chart with 6 skills in rows and 2 columns: 'S1 — I could...' and 'S6 — I can...' — Students write specific examples, not just checkmarks.
activities.facilitation_note: Model the first row on the board. Example: 'Reading — S1: I could read very short sentences with help. S6: I can read a full article about diesel tools and answer comprehension questions.' Modeling gives students the right level of specificity.

activities.activity: Pair share: each student tells their partner one skill they are MOST proud of and one they want to strengthen before the Final Mission. 2 minutes per person.
activities.facilitation_note: Walk the room and listen. You will hear students articulating their own learning — this is metacognition in action. Make mental notes of powerful statements for the whole-class share.

activities.activity: Whole-class share: 2-3 volunteers share their 'most proud' skill. Instructor connects each share to specific evidence or moments from previous sessions. Brief bridge to S7: 'The skills you just named — those are exactly what the Final Mission will test.'
activities.facilitation_note: If no one volunteers, call on a student you heard say something strong during pair share: 'Maria, I heard you say something powerful about your Listening skills. Would you share that with us?' Always ask permission, never force.

formative_checkpoint.method: Scan 'Then vs. Now' charts as students write. Look for: (1) Are they writing specific examples or vague generalities? (2) Are any cells left blank — indicating a skill they feel they did not develop? Flag these students for a brief 1-on-1 during WHILE-D.

differentiation.fast_finishers: Students who complete the chart quickly: on the back, write a 'Letter to S1 Me' — a short message to their Session 1 self about what they have learned. This deepens reflection and creates a meaningful artifact.
differentiation.more_support: Students who struggle to fill in the 'S1' column (they cannot remember what they did NOT know): prompt with specific examples. 'In S1, could you name all 20 Toolbelt words? No? Write that. Now — can you name most of them? Yes? Write that in S6.'

plan_b.risk: Students are emotionally flat after the Cuestionario and do not engage with the reflection
plan_b.mitigation: Start with the Gap Cards activity (high energy, celebratory). If the room is still flat, skip the written chart and do the 'Then vs. Now' as a whole-class oral activity instead: instructor names a skill, students shout one thing they can do now. Movement helps — have them stand for this.

while_c.tecnica_didactica: Diagnóstico por sección / Gráfico de progresión de habilidades (5 dimensiones)

while_d.label: Final Mission Preview + S7 Orientation

teacher_talk.instruction: Alright — let us look ahead. You have proven what you know. Now it is time to prepare for what you will DO. Session 7 is the dress rehearsal. Session 8 is the live performance. The Final Mission is a Workshop Readiness Report — expanded — where ALL five skills are visible. Think of it as everything you have done in this course, combined into one professional performance.

activities.activity: Final Mission brief. Present on the board or distribute a brief card with: task description (expanded Workshop Readiness Report), duration (90-120 seconds per team), evaluation criteria (all 5 language functions visible + grammar accuracy + vocabulary range + fluency), team roles (Carlos/Valentina/Santiago — same as Evidence 5 simulation).

requirements: All 5 language functions must appear in the report
Use at least 10 Toolbelt words correctly
Grammar: at least 2 imperatives, 2 'there is/are' sentences, 2 prepositions of place
brief_card_content.evaluation: Evidence 7 (S7 = practice) + Evidence 8 (S8 = final graded performance)

activities.facilitation_note: Write the brief card content on the board in large letters. Students should copy it into their notebooks. This is their 'mission briefing' — make it feel important. Use a slightly more formal tone: 'This is your professional assignment.'

activities.activity: S7 logistics. Explain: 'In Session 7, you work in teams of 3. Same character roles as the Evidence 5 simulation — Carlos, Valentina, Santiago. You choose your team NOW.' Answer logistical questions: Can we change roles from S5? (Yes.) What if we are absent in S7? (Talk to me today.)
activities.facilitation_note: If the class does not divide evenly into teams of 3, allow one team of 4 (add a second technician: 'Santiago 2') or one team of 2 (the duo handles all roles between them). Be flexible but ensure every student has a team before leaving today.

activities.activity: Team formation. Students form teams of 3 and decide roles. Each team reports to instructor: team members + who plays which character. Instructor records on a class roster.
activities.facilitation_note: Watch for isolated students who are not chosen. If you see someone sitting alone after 3 minutes, step in gently: 'Team 4, you are looking for a third? How about [student name]?' Protect dignity. Every student leaves today with a team.

activities.activity: Initial team planning: 10 minutes for teams to discuss their approach. Guiding questions on board: (1) Which bay will your report describe? (2) Who speaks first, second, third? (3) Which language functions will each person demonstrate? Teams sketch a rough outline — NOT a script.
activities.facilitation_note: Circulate and check that teams are planning, not scripting. If you see a team writing out every word: 'I love the detail, but for the Final Mission, you need to speak naturally — not read. An outline is better than a script. Bullet points, not paragraphs.' This prevents over-reliance on written text and encourages real spoken fluency.

formative_checkpoint.method: Verify that every student is assigned to a team and has a role. Check the roster: are there any names missing? Any team with only 1 person? Resolve before moving to WRAP-UP.

differentiation.fast_finishers: Teams that finish planning early: challenge them to identify which of the 25 Cuestionario questions relates to a language function they will use in the Final Mission. This bridges the assessment to the performance task.
differentiation.more_support: Teams where all members scored low on the Cuestionario (based on your quick scan during break): sit with them for 2 minutes and help them identify the 3 easiest language functions to start with. Build confidence: 'Start with what you know best, then add the harder ones.'

plan_b.risk: Team formation creates conflict or exclusion
plan_b.mitigation: If self-selection causes problems, switch to instructor-assigned teams. Use a simple method: 'Count off 1-2-3 around the room — all 1s are a team, all 2s, all 3s.' This removes social pressure and is perceived as fair. Assign character roles by drawing from a hat.

while_d.tecnica_didactica: Briefing de misión integradora + planeación inicial por equipos

teacher_talk.closing: Six skills. Six evidences. Six sessions. From the very first day — when many of you could not name five tools in English — to today, when you answered twenty-five questions about reading, vocabulary, grammar, listening, and communication functions. Look at where you are. You are ready. Before you leave, I want each of you to write one sentence. Start with: 'In The Diesel Workshop, I can ___.' Fill in the blank with something real — something you could not do before this course. Post it on the Progress Wall on your way out.

activities.activity: Celebration moment. Instructor addresses the class with genuine pride. Acknowledge the difficulty of S6 (a full 90-minute closed-book assessment) and the maturity with which students handled it.
activities.facilitation_note: This is not a generic 'good job.' Name specifics: 'I saw students who struggled with grammar in S3 answering those questions with confidence today. I saw students who were nervous about listening in S4 remembering exact lines from the dialogue. That is real growth, and you earned it.'

activities.activity: Individual writing: one sentence starting with 'In The Diesel Workshop, I can ___.' Provide small cards or sticky notes. Students write, then post on the Progress Wall (a designated wall space or poster).
activities.facilitation_note: Have the cards/sticky notes pre-cut and ready. A stack on each table speeds this up. If you do not have a designated Progress Wall, use the back of the classroom door or a large sheet of chart paper labeled 'WE CAN.' The visual accumulation of statements is the point — one card alone is nice, twenty cards together are powerful.

activities.activity: Instructor reads 2-3 'I can' statements aloud (anonymous — do not say whose card it is unless they volunteer). The class listens. Brief applause or acknowledgment after each one.
activities.facilitation_note: Choose cards that represent different skills — one about vocabulary, one about speaking, one about grammar. If a card is particularly moving or specific, let your genuine reaction show. 'Listen to this one: In The Diesel Workshop, I can describe a safety hazard using There is and a preposition. That is a REAL technical English skill.'

activities.activity: Brief S7 preview: 'Next session — Session 7 — is Final Mission Preparation. Come with your team. Come with your outline. Come ready to perform. And bring your Communication Card — you will need it this time.' Distribute autonomous work instructions. Dismiss.
activities.facilitation_note: End with energy and forward momentum. The last thing they hear should make them want to come back: 'In S7, you stop being students and start being professionals. See you there.'

plan_b.risk: Students rush out before writing their 'I can' statement
plan_b.mitigation: Make it a ticket to leave: 'Your exit ticket today is one sentence on a card. Post it on the wall, then you are free to go.' Stand near the door and give a fist bump or handshake as they post. This small ritual creates closure.

materials_checklist: Cuestionario Consolidado forms — printed, one per student, stapled
Evidence 5 (Escala de estimacion No 5) — graded, with individual written comments
Gap Cards from S1 — plastified, stored — instructor brings them (do NOT distribute)
Then vs. Now chart — printed or drawn on board
Final Mission brief cards — printed or written on board
Sticky notes or small cards for 'I can' statements
Class roster for team formation recording
Chart paper for Progress Wall (if not already designated)
room_setup: Individual desks — exam configuration (no pairs, no groups) for WHILE-A
Word Wall covered or turned to face the wall before students arrive
Communication Cards collected from desks before students arrive
Progress Wall space cleared and labeled
After WHILE-A: desks can be rearranged into pairs/groups for WHILE-B through WRAP-UP
technology: No technology required for the Cuestionario (paper-based)
Optional: projector for displaying answers during WHILE-B review (not required — board works fine)
No audio playback needed — Listening section tests recall, not live listening

session_level_contingencies.risk: Significant number of students arrive late (miss SET-UP)
session_level_contingencies.mitigation: Have a 'Late Arrival' protocol: late students sit at a designated desk near the door, receive their Cuestionario form, write name/date, and begin immediately. They receive the full 90 minutes from their start time (track individually). Brief them on ICQ conditions in a 30-second whisper.

session_level_contingencies.risk: Power outage or facility emergency during the Cuestionario
session_level_contingencies.mitigation: If the outage is brief (<10 min): students wait, add lost time to their 90 minutes. If extended: collect all forms, note the time each student stopped, and resume in the next available session. Do NOT cancel the Cuestionario — it is the only evidence where all 5 skills are assessed.

session_level_contingencies.risk: Students finish the Cuestionario much faster than expected (under 60 min)
session_level_contingencies.mitigation: If most students finish by 08:30, call time at 08:35 (give stragglers 5 more minutes), then extend WHILE-B to include more discussion and examples. Use the extra time for deeper answer explanations and additional practice examples per question.

session_level_contingencies.risk: Emotional distress — a student becomes visibly upset during or after the Cuestionario
session_level_contingencies.mitigation: Approach calmly and quietly. Offer to step outside for 2 minutes. Reassure: 'This Cuestionario is one part of your evaluation — you have five other evidences that show your skills. One hard quiz does not erase everything you have done.' If the student cannot continue, allow them to finish during autonomous time or a makeup session.

instructor_self_check.question: Did I collect ALL Cuestionario forms before beginning the answer review? (If even one student still had their form during WHILE-B, the assessment integrity is compromised.)
During the answer review, did I explain WHY each answer is correct — citing the specific text, dialogue line, or grammar rule — rather than just revealing the letter?
Did every student leave today assigned to a team with a character role for the Final Mission? (Check the roster — any gaps mean a student will arrive at S7 without a team.)

Did the Gap Cards activity in WHILE-C create a genuine moment of recognition — did students visibly react to how much they have learned? (If not, consider which statements to choose differently next time.)

Did the session end on a high note — with energy, pride, and anticipation for S7? (If students left quietly or deflated, the WRAP-UP celebration moment may need to be more personal and specific next time.)

skills_progression_update.note: After S6, all 7 skill areas have been formally assessed. S7-S8 focus on integrated performance (Final Mission).

feeds_from: S1 — Gap Cards (used in WHILE-C preview)
S2 — Reading text 'Tools Every Diesel Technician Needs' (Cuestionario Reading section)
S3 — Grammar structures: Imperatives, There is/are, Prepositions (Cuestionario Grammar section)
S4 — Bay 2 Safety Briefing dialogue (Cuestionario Listening section)
S5 — 5 Language Functions (Cuestionario Language Functions section)
S5 — Evidence 5 (returned at start of S6)
feeds_into: S7 — Final Mission Preparation (teams formed in S6, outlines started, autonomous work feeds directly into S7 rehearsal)
S8 — The Full Circle (Gap Cards redistributed, Final Mission performed, course closure)

justificacion_didactica: El Cuestionario Consolidado No 6 actúa como instrumento de indagación sobre el propio aprendizaje. La revisión colectiva de respuestas y el diagnóstico por sección promueven la metacognición y la construcción crítica del conocimiento sobre las brechas restantes.

grammar_groups: Todos los grupos introducidos (1, 2, 5, 7): evaluación integrada.
Foco en Grupo 1 (be) y Grupo 2 (there is/are) — mayor peso en el cuestionario.
Repaso de Grupo 5 (imperativos) en ejercicio de escritura.

feedback.mode: ACCURACY — sesión de evaluación. Feedback post-cuestionario, no durante.
accuracy_techniques: CERO feedback durante el Cuestionario Consolidado (Evidence 6).
Post-cuestionario: revisión colectiva con respuestas en proyector. Explicación de cada ítem.
Metalinguistic cue al revisar: nombrar la regla gramatical asociada a cada error frecuente.
Corrección explícita permitida durante el repaso — no es producción, es consolidación.
fluency_techniques: Review games (si hay tiempo extra): modo fluency para reducir ansiedad post-cuestionario.
Conversación de cierre de guía: modo fluency, celebrar progreso.
feedback.notes: Orden crítico: (1) Cuestionario en silencio, (2) recoger todos los cuestionarios, (3) SOLO ENTONCES proyectar respuestas. Nunca dar respuestas antes de recoger.

l1_management.l1_percentage: ≤ 10 % L1. Meta: aprendices responden el cuestionario en inglés sin apoyo L1.
l1_management.english_zone_declaration: English Zone máxima durante el cuestionario. Solo instructor puede usar L1 para aclarar instrucciones de formato.
l1_allowed_for: Instrucciones de formato del cuestionario (número de respuestas, tiempo).
Situación de emergencia o confusión total de algún aprendiz.
l1_management.reduction_strategy: Logro de S6: que el aprendiz pueda leer, entender y responder preguntas técnicas en inglés sin traducción. Celebrar este hito explícitamente.

techniques: No hay drill de pronunciación en S6 — es sesión de evaluación escrita.
Si hay tiempo en el repaso: lectura coral de oraciones correctas del cuestionario para refuerzo fonológico.
stress_pronunciation.notes: Pronunciación se retoma en S7 con foco en la presentación oral de la Final Mission.

factors_applied: E — Encounter again: todos los términos del Toolbelt aparecen en el cuestionario.
S — Self-expression: ítem de escritura libre — aprendiz describe el taller en 3 oraciones.
